pull.title: rpc: handle malformed jsonrpc 2.0 requests correctly
pull.body:
While reviewing #36642 I found something else we missed in JSON-RPC 2.0:

If we receive a malformed request we would assume that we couldn't parse it's jsonrpc version and send an HTTP error.  This is how the legacy jsonrpc server worked (despite that behavior not ever being part of any ratified jsonrpc spec) and we maintain it as Bitcoin "legacy" jsonrpc protocol. However it's possible to form a request that does properly indicate jsonrpc 2.0 but is still malformed. In that case, we should not send an HTTP error: the correct protocol is to respond with `HTTP 200 OK` and include the jsonrpc error message in the response.

The solution is to check if we know the request's jsonrpc version before responding with an error.

We already correctly handle such malformed requests in batches and this is already tested in `test_batch_requests()` in `interface_rpc.py`

On master, the functional test in this PR actually crashes the node because the assumption is codified. Note that this crash requires:
1. RPC Authentication
2. A debug build

So this is not an urgent security fix, but a bug that might disrupt testing.

```
node0 stderr httprpc.cpp:46
    UniValue JSONErrorReply(UniValue, const JSONRPCRequest &, HTTPStatusCode &):
        'jreq.m_json_version != JSONRPCVersion::V2' check failed.
```


In release builds the node doesn't crash, but it returns HTTP 400 with a JSON-RPC 2.0 error body instead of HTTP 200.

push to f5ed688fa1379c3703764538a27d66266e758968

- rebase on master after merge of #36642 
- fix handling of batches with malformed requests, added an extra commit with @ryanofsky as coauthor

tACK f5ed688fa1379c3703764538a27d66266e758968

ryanofsky asked that batches follow the same notification rule as single requests, and the new commit decides it in `parse()`, as he suggested. I reran the probe from my last review on regtest (https://gist.github.com/fametrano/e5ebd604b25ed609b7144e53c1a23a5e/bf392bb18cdd5312a1607e09f466b75ccaab7852), with the previous head on the same master as the baseline.

The six malformed 2.0 requests of the test still get HTTP 200 with the error. For a user without a whitelist, a batch element without an id that fails to parse, such as `{"jsonrpc":"2.0"}`, had no reply before and now gets its error with `"id":null`. Valid notifications, alone or in a batch, still get 204 with no body. `interface_rpc.py`, `rpc_whitelist.py`, `interface_http.py` and `rpc_users.py` pass.

Code review ACK f5ed688fa1379c3703764538a27d66266e758968. On master, a malformed JSON-RPC 2.0 request makes debug builds abort and gets an HTTP 400 in release builds. With this PR it gets an HTTP 200 reply with the error, as the spec requires, and invalid requests without an id now get an error reply instead of being treated as notifications, both alone and in batches.

Thanks for the updates and for rebasing on #36642. The main remaining suggestion is to add commit messages to the [second](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36758#discussion_r4564223263) and [third](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36758#discussion_r4564223454) commits saying what behavior they change. The other comments are small test nits and can be ignored.

events.message:
rpc: handle malformed jsonrpc 2.0 requests correctly

Return HTTP 200 with an error reply for invalid JSON-RPC 2.0 requests,
such as ones with no method or with invalid params, like other 2.0
errors. Previously these requests hit an Assume() that aborted debug
builds, and release builds replied with HTTP 400.

JSONErrorReply() now handles 2.0 requests instead of asserting it never
gets them. Replies to requests without an "id" now include "id": null,
as JSON-RPC 2.0 requires.

rpc: requests that fail to parse can not be jsonrpc2.0 notifications

Reply with an error to invalid JSON-RPC 2.0 requests without an "id" in
batches, instead of treating them as notifications and returning HTTP 204.
JSON-RPC 2.0 only treats _valid_ requests without an id as notifications.
This change keeps batch behavior consistent with nonbatch behavior after
previous commit which started returning error replies for invalid single
requests.

Co-authored-by: Ryan Ofsky <ryan@ofsky.org>

comments.body:
In commit "rpc: handle malformed jsonrpc 2.0 requests correctly" (02380237ddd2ed6878d7a3b0ae2807cfcf2cd9ff)

Not a blocker, but if we want to comply with the spec it seems like this case should get an error reply instead of 204. The JSON-RPC 2.0 spec's [examples](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#examples) answer an invalid Request object with no id (`{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": 1, "params": "bar"}`) with an error and `"id": null`, treating it as an invalid request rather than a notification. If we don't want to comply with the spec, the test comment should be updated to say this is intentional. The [test comment suggestion](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36758#discussion_r4472774752) includes that.

Note that compatibility with previous bitcoin core releases shouldn't be a concern in this case since before this PR this request made debug builds abort on the `Assume` in `JSONErrorReply()`, and release builds returned HTTP 400 with a "Missing method" error and no id.

comments.body:
In commit "rpc: handle malformed jsonrpc 2.0 requests correctly" (02380237ddd2ed6878d7a3b0ae2807cfcf2cd9ff)

Since this commit only adds test cases, it's hard to tell from the diff what behavior it changes. Could the commit message say what these requests did before? The PR description explains it, but the commit only has a subject line. Something like:

```
A JSON-RPC 2.0 request that fails to parse after its "jsonrpc": "2.0" field
has been read, for example one with a missing or non-string method or
invalid params, reached the Assume in JSONErrorReply(). Debug builds
aborted, and release builds returned HTTP 400 with a 2.0 error body.

Return these errors like any other 2.0 error instead: HTTP 200 with the
error in the reply, or HTTP 204 and no reply for a request without an id.
```

The test comments could explain more too. The [notification case](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/02380237ddd2ed6878d7a3b0ae2807cfcf2cd9ff/test/functional/interface_rpc.py#L236-L239) confused me most: it wasn't clear why `{"jsonrpc": "2.0"}` fails to parse (it has no `method`), or how this differs from the invalid-notification case just above it, which parses fine and fails when the method runs. Also, since this case doesn't follow the JSON-RPC 2.0 spec (see the [separate comment about it](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36758#discussion_r4472663654)), the test should say so, so the behavior isn't mistaken for what the spec requires. Maybe:

```diff
--- a/test/functional/interface_rpc.py
+++ b/test/functional/interface_rpc.py
@@ -205,7 +205,8 @@ class RPCInterfaceTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         response, status = send_json_rpc(self.nodes[0], {"jsonrpc": "3.0", "method": "getblockcount"})
         assert_equal(response, {"result": None, "error": {"code": RPC_INVALID_REQUEST, "message": "JSON-RPC version not supported"}})
         assert_equal(status, 400)
-        # invalid requests that are known to be 2.0 get RPC errors but not HTTP errors
+        # Malformed requests that are known to be JSON-RPC 2.0, because they
+        # have "jsonrpc": "2.0", get RPC errors with HTTP 200, not HTTP errors.
         for request, message in [
             ({}, "Missing method"),
             ({"method": 1}, "Method must be a string"),
@@ -233,7 +234,11 @@ class RPCInterfaceTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
         expect_http_rpc_status(204, None, self.nodes[0], "generatetoaddress", [1, "invalid_address"], 2, True)
         # Sanity check: command was not executed
         assert_equal(block_count + 1, self.nodes[0].getblockcount())
-        # No error response for notifications that fail to parse either
+        # No response either for a request without an id that fails to parse,
+        # here because it has no method, so the error happens before any method
+        # runs. This does not follow the JSON-RPC 2.0 spec, which treats an
+        # invalid request as not being a notification and replies with an error
+        # and "id": null.
         response, status = send_json_rpc(self.nodes[0], {"jsonrpc": "2.0"})
         assert_equal(response, None)
         assert_equal(status, 204)
```
Much better approach thanks, taking.

In commit "rpc: requests that fail to parse can not be jsonrpc2.0 notifications" (f5ed688fa1379c3703764538a27d66266e758968)

The log message says this batch is all notifications, which is inaccurate after this commit: the batch has always included the invalid `{"pizza": "sausage"}` request, which used to be dropped as a notification and now gets an error reply. Maybe the message could just say the requests have no ids.

Also, `format_response()` already adds the `jsonrpc` and `error` fields from the call's expected result, so only the id is needed in `response_fields` and this could be simplified to:

```suggestion
        self.log.info("Testing JSON-RPC 2.0 batch of requests without ids...")
        # The request with no method (index 4) is invalid, so it is not a
        # notification, and gets an error reply with "id": null.
        self.test_batch_request(lambda idx: BatchOptions(version=2, notification=True, response_fields={"id": None} if idx == 4 else None))
```

In commit "rpc: handle malformed jsonrpc 2.0 requests correctly" (5004f241c58113fbc29ddd2dbda3af0040827e90)

Could this commit and the next one have messages saying what behavior they change? It would be nice to be able to read the log and know how the server behaved before and after each change, without having to read the PR or the spec. Maybe something like:

```
Return HTTP 200 with an error reply for invalid JSON-RPC 2.0 requests,
such as ones with no method or with invalid params, like other 2.0
errors. Previously these requests hit an Assume() that aborted debug
builds, and release builds replied with HTTP 400.

JSONErrorReply() now handles 2.0 requests instead of asserting it never
gets them. Replies to requests without an "id" now include "id": null,
as JSON-RPC 2.0 requires.
```

And for the next commit, see [the separate comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36758#discussion_r4564223454).

In commit "rpc: requests that fail to parse can not be jsonrpc2.0 notifications" (f5ed688fa1379c3703764538a27d66266e758968)

Suggested message for this commit (see [the comment about the previous one](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36758#discussion_r4564223263)):

```
Reply with an error to invalid JSON-RPC 2.0 requests without an "id" in
batches, instead of treating them as notifications and returning HTTP 204.
JSON-RPC 2.0 only treats _valid_ requests without an id as notifications.
This change keeps batch behavior consistent with nonbatch behavior after
previous commit which started returning error replies for invalid single
requests.
```

In commit "rpc: requests that fail to parse can not be jsonrpc2.0 notifications" (f5ed688fa1379c3703764538a27d66266e758968)

nit: Since `response_fields` now also decides whether a request without an id expects a reply, `is None` seems more accurate than `not`. That way only an unset value means "no reply", and `response_fields={}` means "expect a reply with no extra fields" instead of being treated like `None`:

```suggestion
    if options.version == 2 and options.notification and options.response_fields is None:
```
